question: A 58-year-old woman comes to the physician because of headaches for 1 month. She describes them as 7 out of 10 in intensity. She has no nausea. Two years ago, she was treated for invasive lobular carcinoma of the left breast. She underwent a left mastectomy and multiple cycles of chemotherapy. She has been in good health since this treatment. Her temperature is 37°C (98.6°F), pulse is 90/min, and blood pressure is 118/72 mm Hg. There is a well-healed scar on the left side of the chest. There is no lymphadenopathy. The abdomen is soft and nontender; there is no organomegaly. Neurologic examination shows no focal findings. An MRI of the brain shows a 4-cm temporal hyperintense mass near the surface of the brain. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "58-year-old woman with headaches" -> "History of invasive lobular carcinoma and chemotherapy" -> "Increased risk of brain metastasis" -> 80% CHAIN: "MRI shows 4-cm temporal hyperintense mass near the brain surface" -> "Suspicion of brain metastasis" -> "Need for tissue diagnosis" -> 85% CHAIN: "No focal neurologic findings on examination" -> "Less likely to be a primary brain tumor" -> "Higher suspicion for metastasis" -> 75% CHAIN: "Well-healed scar on the left side of the chest" -> "Previous history of left breast cancer" -> "Potential for metastatic spread to the brain" -> 80%
analysis: The most appropriate next step in management for the 4-cm temporal hyperintense mass near the surface of the brain in this patient with a history of invasive lobular carcinoma of the left breast is likely to be surgical resection to obtain tissue for histologic diagnosis and to relieve mass effect symptoms.
